studies.name: Service galleries
studies.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Make a polished environmental concept paintover for a stylized three.js video-game town menu called Respite, a maintained human settlement inside enormous inherited machine infrastructure. No people or robots.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the ACTUAL 3D LAYOUT, whose camera, framing, building footprints, entrance orientations and main silhouettes are fixed. Image 2 is a reference for coherent inhabited sci-fi architecture and separation of buildings from background, NOT layout. Image 3 is a reference ONLY for matte scuffed painterly material treatment and economical simple beveled geometry, NOT its orange palette, characters, text or arena. Image 4 is reference ONLY for mysterious machine scale and layered fog, NOT its bright central glow, green palette or people.
LOCK the five destinations from image 1: left foreground reinforced stash vault with partly open leaf opens RIGHT toward the court; rear-left compact Codex with twin angled front fins opens toward the court; rear-center-right circular cyan exit with observation tower on its RIGHT stays embedded in a continuous huge wall; rear-right workshop has ONE boiler-like drum and pipes; right foreground broad three-wing horseshoe bazaar opens LEFT into the SAME court and retains BOTH entrance return walls and all three roofed wings, with supported plum fabric awnings. Preserve habitable depth, entrance scale, and clear sight of workshop doorway behind market. No freestanding sixth destination.
The arrival story must be immediate: emerge from the tunnel directly into a common civic court; stash and market face each other across it, with Codex and workshop around the back. Clear short routes, continuous ground, quiet open central/foreground paving. No foreground wall, cliff, water, bridge, center statue, vehicle or clutter.
The task is environmental design and atmosphere around these fixed assets, NOT a wholesale replacement of them. Add believable connections and a restrained background, especially left. Dark navy and blue-violet atmosphere, selective cyan, lilac and amber practical light; dark neutral scuffed paint, sparse surviving colour. Use low-frequency painted wear and simple game-model geometry; NO high fidelity micro-greebles, fine scratches, tin shelves, photoreal materials, glossy wet floor, repeated neon outlines, orange/teal toy panels, or tiny merchandise. Fog separates distant layers; foreground materials stay visible. Exit has strongest focal contrast; other destinations remain legible and distinct. Broad forms and selective detail, high-quality game art.
Output one landscape composition matching image 1 aspect, no labels, typography, watermark or UI.
STUDY A — SERVICE GALLERIES. Make the plaza feel built into an inhabited perimeter. Integrate the plain left service block into a shallow run of utility rooms behind the stash and Codex, with one coherent supported gallery above them that connects to the existing habitat wall. A second distant gallery fades into blue fog. Use a few grouped opaque warm windows and two restrained plum fabric accents as signs of care. Sparse conduits terminate at meaningful services. Low continuous bases and paving joins unite the buildings without separate raised islands. Keep these connectors subordinate to the five destinations. Warm local pools against deep navy shade, cyan passage light softly reaching into the court. Mood: inhabited refuge within a vast indifferent machine.

STUDY B — CURVED STRUCTURAL RIBS. The town occupies a small inhabited pocket at the base of an enormous curved shell. Above and behind the five unchanged buildings, one giant partial structural rib rises from the rear LEFT and sweeps beyond the TOP of the image; it is a fragment of a much larger machine, not a second gate and not a canopy over the plaza. Make the wall feel deep and layered with two broad curved structural bands fading into dark blue-violet fog. The circular exit remains in its same flat lower wall and the wall continues past the RIGHT edge. At ground level, a low continuous maintenance plinth and sparse thick connected utility runs bind the rear-left block to the Codex, and the rear-right workshop to the wall. Prioritize large simple masses and negative space. No dense galleries, no extra window grids, no added shopfronts, no vegetation borders or foreground plants. Restrained lilac rim light from the LEFT distance; warmer human entrances below; cyan gate brightest. Keep the human court inviting but small beside the inherited structure. Controlled geometric design, broad dry matte scuffs. Do not alter any main building footprint or direction.

STUDY C — SHARED UTILITY STRUCTURE. Give the plaza a physically connected machine-world identity through one substantial old utility trunk in the BACKGROUND. A large horizontal dark conduit emerges from beyond the LEFT frame, travels behind the low service block and Codex, and seats into a heavy junction in the rear wall left of the exit, with two restrained thinner branches following the perimeter to the buildings. Place its supports behind the destinations, never in the central court. The existing workshop roof pipes visibly connect to inherited wall infrastructure. Above, huge staggered dark service masses recede into low-contrast violet-blue fog; sparse distant cyan signals, no window grid, no repeated residential balconies. The near buildings have mostly charcoal and slate paint, very few coloured panels, and soft scuffs. Warm light stays confined to entrances, workshop amber slit, and market awnings; Codex keeps a small lilac slit. Deep shadow fills the space between light pools. The five destinations stand out clearly. No vegetation, no steam obscuring the building fronts, no foreground structure or overhead pipes crossing the camera. Keep the existing planar court ground and all building forms and entrances fixed. The atmosphere suggests a functioning place people maintain inside a much older machine, not a ruined factory.
